text: Fubini's theorem says: for non-negative measurable f on X×Y,
choices: ∫_{X×Y} f d(μ×ν) = ∫_X(∫_Y f dν)dμ = ∫_Y(∫_X f dμ)dν (iterated integrals equal the double integral)
the iterated integrals need not be equal
explanation: Fubini-Tonelli: for f≥0, all three integrals are equal. For general f, the same holds if f is integrable. Order of integration can be exchanged.
